title: Onana pens new Aston Villa deal: It's been amazing so far
subtitle: Amadou Onana is set to miss most of the season due to a serious knee injury, but he has penned a new contract with Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Amadou Onana is relishing the opportunity to extend his stay at Aston Villa after he signed a new deal with Unai Emery's team.
Onana joined Villa from Everton for a reported £50m in 2024, and has made 72 appearances for the Villans, scoring seven goals.
However, the 25-year-old is out for the majority of this campaign after he sustained a cruciate ligament injury.
Yet that has not stopped Villa from offering the Belgium international fresh terms, and he is thrilled to stay on.
"Everyone at this football club just made me feel so welcome, from the first day – the staff, the players," Onana said.
"The fans, I obviously have a very special connection with them as well, so it means a lot for me to be able to renew my contract.
"[Unai is] very important – he's the main man. If we are in this position, this situation we are in, it's thanks to him.

"He's done incredible things at this football club, four years in a row in Europe, winning a Europa League in the third year, I think that's something very special and we all have to thank him for that.

"If I'm renewing and re-signing a new deal, I must be enjoying it! It's been amazing so far. They've definitely improved me as a player and made me a better player, so I'm grateful to them, but there's still a lot of work to do.
"It's a big one for me, for the club to take the initiative to renew my contract while I'm recovering from such a big injury, it means a lot.

"It's definitely made me a lot stronger, and I learned a lot about myself as well. Sometimes it gets dark, and that's when you need those people around you – people from here, the staff – but I'm very grateful for how it's going so far. I can't wait to be back."
Villa sit 10th in the Premier League ahead of facing Sunderland on Saturday.
Aston Villa - Nicolas Jackson
Only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (seven) have scored more Premier League goals this season than Jackson (six), who has netted in each of his last three games.
Across his 132 games in Europe's big five leagues, only in April/May 2023 for Villarreal has Jackson scored in four in a row.
Sunderland - Brian Brobbey

Among players with at least 450 minutes in the Premier League this season, Brobbey is one of three players to have both won (2.0) and conceded (1.9) more than 1.8 fouls per 90, along with Abdul Fatawu and Boubacar Kamara.
He is Sunderland's joint-leading scorer in the league this term, but all three of his goals came against Manchester City in September.
MATCH PREDICTION: ASTON VILLA WIN
Emery is set to take charge of his 150th Premier League game for Villa (W76 D33 L40), becoming the second manager to do so for them in the competition, after Martin O'Neill (P152 W61 D53 L38).
Of the 42 instances in the Premier League of a manager having at least 149 games at a club, Emery at Villa ranks 10th for both win rate (51.0%) and points per game (1.75).

Villa are unbeaten in their last six league games (W3 D3), though those three draws saw the Villans drop six points from winning positions – it is the joint-most of any Premier League side since the start of October, along with Hull City.
Sunderland, meanwhile, are winless in their last seven away league games against Villa (D4 L3), since a 1-0 win in January 2011.
Villa have lost just one of their last 12 Premier League games against Sunderland (W5 D6), going down 3-1 at the Stadium of Light in January 2016.
Sunderland are looking to win successive Premier League games for the first time this season, having previously done so in their final two matches of 2025-26.
